citation: Kawabata A, Sawayama S. A study on the content of pectic substances in vegetables. Jpn J Nutr Diet. 1973;31(1):32-36, Table 3
unit: per cent of the fresh edible portion, which is g/100 g and is the unit the pectin column already holds
analyte: total pectin as calcium pectate, the sum of three sequential extraction fractions: water-soluble at 30 C, 0.4 per cent sodium hexametaphosphate at 30 C, and 0.05 N hydrochloric acid at 85 C. This is an operationally defined measure, not a modern molecularly defined pectin assay, and cells drawn from it mean what this method means.
note: Twenty-four vegetables, open access on J-STAGE, and the answer to a column that had one figure in it after four rounds of searching. Its English abstract reports only banded categories, 2 per cent or over, 1.00 to 1.99, 0.50 to 0.99, 0.10 to 0.49, and every secondary account of this paper repeats those bands. Table 3 carries the actual per-food figures and is what is transcribed here.
reading: Table 3 is a scanned image with no text layer, so it was read visually rather than parsed. The Japanese summary also lists okra in the 1.00 to 1.99 band where the English abstract omits it, which is a second reason not to work from the abstract.
why-raw-only: The paper measures fresh vegetables. Only page foods that are themselves raw are mapped. Pumpkin, okra, aubergine, green beans, edamame, lotus root, taro, potato and yam are all in this table and all cooked on the page, and a fresh figure against a cooked row is the mismatch this store refuses everywhere else.

rows.note: W-S recorded as a trace by the source
Assayed in three parts along the root, tip 0.303, middle 0.333 and base 0.319, so the cell is a range over them rather than a point. The paper says the differences were slight.

unmapped.note: Also in Table 3 and reaching no page food, or reaching one in the wrong state.

companion: Kawabata A, Sawayama S, Uryu K. A study on the contents of pectic substances in fruits, vegetable fruits and nuts. Jpn J Nutr Diet. 1974;32(1):9-18, doi 10.5264/eiyogakuzashi.32.9. Same method, same fresh edible portion basis, fifty foods, and its Table 6 covers avocado, banana, pineapple, mango, papaya, apple, pear, tomato, watermelon, chestnut, walnut and peanut, several of them raw on this page. Fetched and confirmed to exist; not transcribed here because its food names run vertically down the left column of a scan and reading them wrongly would put a real figure on the wrong food.
